'''Desmond Michael Bane''' (born June 25, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Orlando Magic]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU Horned Frogs]]. 

A [[shooting guard]], Bane was selected in the first round of the [[2020 NBA draft]] with the 30th overall pick by the [[Boston Celtics]], but was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in November 2020 before the start of his rookie season. He was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] in his first year in the NBA. In June 2025, Bane was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=June 15, 2025 |title=Orlando Magic Acquire Desmond Bane From Memphis |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-acquire-desmond-bane-memphis-grizzlies-release-20250615 |access-date=June 15, 2025 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

==Early life==
Until he was two, Desmond, his sister, and his mother, Marissa, moved often. At age two, he moved to [[Richmond, Indiana]]<ref name="jimenez">{{cite web |last=Jiménez |first=Jesús |title=Great-grandparents molded Seton Catholic star |url=https://www.pal-item.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/03/26/great-grandparents-molded-seton-catholic-star/81989968/ |website=[[Palladium-Item]] |access-date=December 4, 2019 |date=March 26, 2016}}</ref> to live with his great-grandparents. At age 13, he discovered that his father, Etieno Ekiko, lived in [[Nigeria]].<ref name="davison">{{cite web |last=Davison |first=Drew |title=Overlooked? Counted out? Desmond Bane knows what TCU is facing all too well |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article227469919.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=December 4, 2019 |date=March 13, 2019}}</ref> He focused on playing baseball until eighth grade, with his great-grandfather coaching at the youth level. He also played football and soccer.<ref name=jimenez/> 

==High school career==
Desmond Bane played basketball for [[Seton Catholic High School (Richmond, Indiana)|Seton Catholic High School]], a small [[private school]] in [[Richmond, Indiana]].<ref name=jimenez/> He played there under head coach Josh Jurgens.<ref name="CommercialAppeal">{{cite news |last=Cole |first=Damichael |title=Explaining Desmond Bane's meteoric rise with Memphis Grizzlies |url=https://eu.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/nba/grizzlies/2022/02/07/memphis-grizzlies-desmond-bane-one-nba-top-second-year-players/6654853001/ |work=The Commercial Appeal |date=February 7, 2022}}</ref> As a senior, Bane averaged a state-high 30 points, 11.5 rebounds, 6.1 assists and 3.2 blocks per game. He scored a school-record 62 points and nine three-pointers in a win over [[Lincoln Senior High School (Cambridge City, Indiana)|Lincoln Senior High School]].<ref name="jimenez2">{{cite web |last=Jiménez |first=Jesús |title=8 unforgettable Desmond Bane moments |url=https://www.pal-item.com/story/sports/college/2018/03/13/8-unforgettable-desmond-bane-moments/421417002/ |website=[[Palladium-Item]] |access-date=December 4, 2019 |date=March 13, 2018}}</ref> 

He was named MVP of the Wettig Memorial Holiday Tournament. Bane scored 1,991 points over his four-year career, surpassing 1988 [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] winner Woody Austin for the most in [[Wayne County, Indiana|Wayne County]] history. 
He did not receive an [[NCAA Division I]] offer until his senior season, when [[Furman Paladins men's basketball|Furman]] offered him at the end of the November early-signing period.<ref name="CommercialAppeal" /> On May 12, 2016, Bane committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|Texas Christian University]] (TCU).<ref name="jimenez3">{{cite web |last=Jiménez |first=Jesús |title=How TCU and Desmond Bane became a perfect match |url=https://www.pal-item.com/story/sports/college/2018/03/17/march-madness-2018-how-tcu-and-desmond-bane-became-perfect-match/434658002/ |website=[[Palladium-Item]] |access-date=December 5, 2019 |date=March 17, 2018}}</ref> He was not rated by major recruiting services [[247Sports]], [[ESPN]], or [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].<ref name=davison/>

==College career==
[[File:Desmond Bane 3.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Bane with [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]] in 2020]]
Bane earned [[Big 12]] Newcomer of the Week honors after scoring 18 points and pulling down seven rebounds against [[2016–17 Bradley Braves men's basketball team|Bradley]]. He had 16 points including three free throws with two seconds remaining to help TCU defeat number one-ranked [[2016–17 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]], 85–82, in the quarterfinals of the Phillips 66 Big 12 Championship. Bane helped TCU win the NIT as a freshman, contributing nine points in the title game against [[2016–17 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]]. He averaged 7.1 points and 2.9 rebounds per game and making 13 starts. In an 89–83 victory over [[2016–17 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]], Bane scored a season-high 27 points. As a sophomore, Bane averaged 12.5 points and 4.1 rebounds per game and his 47.2% three-point accuracy led the Big 12. In the NCAA tournament, Bane had five points, four rebounds, four assists, a steal and a block in the first-round loss to [[2017–18 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]].<ref name="jimenez3"/> As a junior, Bane was named to the second-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Lopez |first=Selby |title=Baylor stars earn multiple All-Big 12 honors. See the full list of conference award winners |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/2019/03/10/baylor-stars-earn-multiple-all-big-12-honors-see-the-full-list-of-conference-award-winners/ |access-date=December 6, 2019 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |date=March 10, 2019}}</ref> He had a career-high 34 points in the team's regular-season finale against [[2018–19 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]] and scored 30 points versus [[2018–19 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] in the second round of the NIT. Bane averaged 15.2 points per game to lead the team, 5.7 rebounds per game and shot 42.5% from behind the arc. After the season, he "tested the waters" of the NBA draft but returned to TCU.<ref>{{cite news |last=Straka |first=Dean |title=TCU leading-scorer Desmond Bane to enter name in draft, test NBA waters |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/2019/04/10/tcu-leading-scorer-desmond-bane-to-enter-name-in-draft-test-nba-waters/ |access-date=December 6, 2019 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |date=April 10, 2019}}</ref> As a senior, Bane was named to the first-team All-Big 12.<ref name="Big 12 awards">{{cite press release|url=https://big12sports.com/news/2020/3/7/mens-basketball-all-big-12-awards-announced.aspx|title=Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced|work=[[Big 12 Conference]]|date=March 8, 2020 |access-date=March 8, 2020}}</ref> Bane averaged 16.6 points and 6.3 rebounds per game, and his 44.2% three-point accuracy led the Big 12. On March 2, 2020, Bane was named Big 12 player of the week after scoring 23 points in a 75–72 upset over second-ranked [[2019–20 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://big12sports.com/news/2020/3/2/tcu-texas-collect-mens-basketball-weekly-awards.aspx|title=TCU, Texas Collect Men's Basketball Weekly Awards|publisher=Big 12 Conference|date=March 2, 2020|access-date=March 2, 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Memphis Grizzlies (2020–2025)===
Bane was selected with the 30th pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]]. He became the first TCU player to be picked in the first round since [[Kurt Thomas (basketball)|Kurt Thomas]] in [[1995 NBA draft|1995]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Griffith |first=Katherine |title=TCU's Desmond Bane selected in first round of NBA draft, reportedly heading to Memphis Grizzlies via trade |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/tcu-horned-frogs/2020/11/18/desmond-bane-becomes-tcus-second-all-time-first-round-pick-first-since-1995/ |access-date=November 19, 2020 |work=[[Dallas Morning News]] |date=November 18, 2020}}</ref> Bane was subsequently traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for a future pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Grizzlies acquire draft rights to Desmond Bane and Mario Hezonja in three-team trade with Celtics and Trail Blazers|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-draft-rights-to-desmond-bane-and-mario-hezonja-in-three-team-trade-with-celtics-and-trail-blazers-201120|date=November 20, 2020|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=November 20, 2020}}</ref> On November 25, 2020, the Grizzlies announced that they had signed Bane.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=November 25, 2020 |title=Grizzlies Sign Desmond Bane To Rookie Contract |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2020/11/grizzlies-sign-desmond-bane-to-rookie-contract.html |access-date=October 27, 2023 |website=HoopsRumors.com}}</ref> Bane was selected to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] after his rookie season. He had the highest three-point field goal percentage in a rookie season since [[Stephen Curry]] (minimum 150 attempts).
[[File:Desmond Bane (51915337353).jpg|thumb|Bane with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the 2022 [[Three-Point Contest]]]]
On December 5, 2021, Bane scored a then-career-high 29 points and had nine rebounds in a 97–90 win over the [[2021–22 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Caplan |first=Callie |title=After torching Mavs, Desmond Bane reflects on draft snub for Josh Green: 'That's on them' |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2021/12/05/after-torching-mavs-ex-tcu-star-desmond-bane-reflects-on-draft-snub-for-josh-green-not-on-me/ |access-date=December 6, 2021 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |date=December 5, 2021}}</ref> Bane and [[Tyrese Haliburton]] were the winners of the Clorox Clutch Challenge at the [[2022 NBA All-Star Game|2022 NBA All Star]] Weekend.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2022 Rising Stars Recap: Haliburton Wins Clutch Challenge|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/2022-rising-stars-recap-tyrese-haliburton-chris-duarte|access-date=2022-02-19|website=NBA.com|language=en}}</ref> On March 23, 2022, Bane set the Grizzlies' franchise record for three-pointers made in a season, surpassing [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)|Mike Miller]]'s record set in 2007 (202).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Postgame Report: Historic night from Desmond Bane helps Grizzlies earn 50th win of the season |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/postgame/bkn-220323# |access-date=March 25, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref>

In the first round of the [[2022 NBA playoffs]] while facing the [[2021–22 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]], on April 22, Bane led Memphis in scoring with 34 points during a 119–118 Game 4 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cole |first=Damichael |date=April 23, 2023 |title=Desmond Bane scores 34, but the Memphis Grizzlies drop Game 4 against the Timberwolves |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/nba/grizzlies/2022/04/23/live-updates-score-game-4-memphis-grizzlies-vs-timberwolves/7356211001 |access-date=October 27, 2023 |website=commercialappeal.com}}</ref> On April 30, Bane scored 23 points to help the Grizzlies eliminate the Timberwolves and reach the second round of the playoffs. Bane made 27 three-pointers in the series and set a new record for most three-pointers in team history during a single postseason.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 30, 2022 |title=Grizzlies rally past Wolves 114-106 to reach 2nd round |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401430234 |access-date=April 30, 2022 |website=ESPN}}</ref> The Grizzlies were eventually eliminated in six games during the second round by the [[2021–22 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]], who went on to win the [[2022 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]].

On October 24, 2022, Bane scored a then-career-high 38 points in a 134–124 win over the [[2022–23 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/grizzlies-news-desmond-banes-stone-cold-reaction-to-dropping-career-high-38-points-vs-nets/|title=Grizzlies guard Desmond Bane's stone cold reaction to dropping career high 38 points vs. Nets|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}}</ref> On November 11, during a 114–103 win over the [[2022–23 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]], he suffered a right foot injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Clay |date=November 12, 2022 |title=MORANT HAS 28 TO POWER GRIZZLIES PAST TIMBERWOLVES, 114-103 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200181 |access-date=March 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Three days later, the Grizzlies announced that Bane was diagnosed with a Grade 2 sprain of his right big toe and would be re-evaluated in 2-to-3 weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=MacMahon |first=Tim |author-link=Tim MacMahon |date=November 15, 2022 |title=Grizzlies' Desmond Bane out at least 2-3 weeks for toe sprain |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/35032401 |access-date=March 16, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On December 7, the Grizzlies announced that Bane was ruled out for another three-to-four weeks with the injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2022 |title=Memphis Grizzlies Medical Update |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-medical-update-12-7-22 |access-date=March 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> However, he made his return ahead of schedule on December 24, recording 17 points, three rebounds and two assists in a 125–100 win over the [[2022–23 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Jack |date=December 24, 2022 |title=BANE RETURNS, GRIZZLIES ROUT BOOKER-LESS SUNS 125-100 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200490 |access-date=March 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

In game 4 of the Grizzlies' first-round playoff series against the [[2022–23 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]], Bane scored a playoff career-high 36 points in a 117–111 overtime loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401541184|title=LeBron leads Lakers past Grizz 117-111 in OT for 3-1 lead|website=ESPN.com|date=April 24, 2023|access-date=April 30, 2023}}</ref> Two days later, Bane recorded 33 points, a playoff career-high 10 rebounds and 5 assists in a 116–99 game 5 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401541231|title=Morant, Grizzlies stave off elimination, beat Lakers 116-99|website=ESPN.cm|date=April 26, 2023|access-date=April 30, 2023}}</ref> Memphis lost the series in 6 games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-28 |title=Lakers obliterate Grizzlies 125-85, advance to 2nd round |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401541232 |access-date=2023-04-30 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>
After the 2022–23 season ended, Bane signed the largest contract in Grizzlies franchise history with a new max extension deal with the Grizzlies, which clocked in at five years for $207 million.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-08 |title=Grizzlies sign Desmond Bane to multi-year contract extension |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-desmond-bane-to-multi-year-contract-extension |access-date=2023-07-17 |website=NBA.com }}</ref>

On December 6, 2023, Bane scored a career-high 49 points, along with six rebounds and eight assists, in a 116–102 win against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hogg |first=Dave |date=December 6, 2023 |title=Desmond Bane scores career-high 49 points, Grizzlies send Pistons to 18th straight loss |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2023/12/06/desmond-bane-scores-career-high-49-points-grizzlies-send-pistons-to-18th-straight-loss/71833380007/ |access-date=2023-12-07 |website=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> He also joined [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)|Mike Miller]] as the only players in Grizzlies history to put up at least 45 points, five rebounds and five assists in a game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/grizzlies-news-desmond-bane-duplicates-feat-not-seen-since-mike-millers-2007-masterpiece|title=Grizzlies' Desmond Bane duplicates feat not seen since Mike Miller's 2007 masterpiece|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=December 6, 2023|access-date=December 6, 2023}}</ref>

On October 2, 2024, Bane was a full participant in training camp after suffering a back injury in the final nine games of the 2023–2024 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Grizzlies' Desmond Bane: Healthy for camp |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-desmond-bane-healthy-for-camp/ |website=CBSSports.com |access-date=2 October 2024 |language=en |date=2 October 2024}}</ref> On March 3, 2025, Bane recorded his first career triple-double with 35 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 132–130 loss against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 4, 2025 |title=LeVert's last-second bucket gives Hawks a 132-130 win over the Grizzlies |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705444 |access-date=March 4, 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2025–present)===
On June 15, 2025, Bane was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] in exchange for [[Kentavious Caldwell-Pope]], [[Cole Anthony]], four unprotected first-round draft picks (2025, 2026, 2028, 2030), and a 2029 first-round pick swap.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 15, 2025 |title=Grizzlies trade Desmond Bane to Magic in blockbuster deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45517668/sources-grizzlies-trade-desmond-bane-magic-blockbuster-deal |access-date=May 4, 2026 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He started all 82 games for the Magic during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 20.1 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 4.1 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Here Are The NBA's 2026-26 Iron Men. How Do They Compare To Years Past?|url=https://www.si.com/nba/iron-men-players-all-82-games-list-compared-years-past|access-date=July 31, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref> On April 25, 2026, in Orlando's Game 3 playoff victory over the [[2025–26 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]], Bane recorded 25 points on 9-of-18 shooting, including 7-of-9 three pointers; his seven three-pointers tied [[Dennis Scott (basketball)|Dennis Scott]]'s franchise record for made threes in a game.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Desmond Bane, Magic hold off Pistons, take 2-1 series lead|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48593209/orlando-magic-hold-detroit-pistons-take-2-1-series-lead|access-date=July 27, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Bane is a devout [[Catholic]]. He is also very involved with the youth in his home town of Richmond, Indiana.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Shaughnessy|first=John|date=February 24, 2021|title=New NBA player credits making it to the pros to his faith, family, school|url=https://www.thebostonpilot.com/article.asp?ID=189445|url-status=live|access-date=March 3, 2021|website=The Boston Pilot|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225172015/https://www.thebostonpilot.com/article.asp?ID=189445 |archive-date=February 25, 2021 }}</ref>

He met his wife, Tatum Talley, during freshman orientation at [[Texas Christian University]]. The two were married in [[Cabo San Lucas|Cabo]], Mexico in September 2024. They have two children.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Copeland |first=Blythe |date=8 January 2026 |title=NBA Star Desmond Bane's Blue and White Wedding on the Beach in Mexico |url=https://www.brides.com/memphis-grizzlies-desmond-bane-wedding-photos-exclusive-megan-kay-photography-8741488 |url-status=live |access-date=29 April 2026 |website=Brides}}</ref>
